concepts.def: Total energy a star emits per second, in watts.
How bright a star looks from Earth.
Mass unit equal to the Sun's mass.
Total time a star spends fusing hydrogen on main sequence.
More massive main sequence stars are much more luminous.

walkthroughs.body_html: Massive stars burn fuel faster and die sooner. A star of 10 solar masses may live only ~30 million years, while a 0.5 solar mass star can last over 100 billion years.
If you double the distance to a star its brightness drops by a factor of 4 (2^2). Triple the distance: brightness drops by 9.
Top-left: hot, luminous, blue stars (e.g., O-type supergiants). Bottom-right: cool, dim, red dwarfs. White dwarfs sit bottom-left; red giants top-right.
